name: Judas
overview: Judas is a male biblical figure identified uniquely as the man at whose house in Damascus Saul, later known as Paul, was staying, as recorded in Acts 9:11. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him. His role is noted within the context of the early Christian community in Damascus.
namesAndTitles: The name Judas means 'praised' in the original language, reflecting a proper name without indication of divine naming, as referenced in Acts 9:11. This meaning aligns with the common usage of the name during the New Testament period.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Judas beyond his association as the host to Saul/Paul in Damascus. No other familial connections are documented in the provided data.
scriptureSignificance: Judas holds significance as the host for Saul during a pivotal moment in the early church, when Saul was transformed into Paul, a foremost apostle to the Gentiles. Although little else is known about Judas, his willingness to provide refuge to Saul situates him within the unfolding of God's redemptive plan through Paul's ministry. This connection indirectly ties him to the broader narrative of salvation history that includes the lineage of Judah, from whom the Messiah, Jesus Christ, would come.
